docs.title: Algorithmic Edge & Mechanical Rules
docs.text:
100% Rule-Based Orderflow Verification

Unlike discretionary methods that leave traders guessing whether a swing was swept or mitigated, the TTrades Fractal Model relies strictly on objective mathematical conditions:

  1. Candle Body Close: A Change in State of Delivery (CISD) requires a solid candle body close past the benchmark open price. Wick probes do NOT qualify.
  2. Origin Accuracy: The CISD benchmark ray begins strictly at the Open of the first opposing candle that initiated the move into the C2 extreme.
  3. Timeframe Fractality: Lower timeframe execution models only trigger inside higher timeframe Points of Interest (FVGs, Orderblocks, or Dealing Range Discount).

docs.title: Common Mistakes & Invalidation Checklist
docs.text: The top 6 fatal errors traders make with the Fractal Model and how to eliminate them.

docs.title: 1. Entering on a Wick Instead of a Candle Body Close
docs.text:
The Fatal Error

A candle wicks through the blue CISD line, and the trader clicks "Buy Market" while the candle is still actively moving. The candle then immediately retracts and closes below the line, trapping the trader.

  • The Rule: You must wait for the countdown timer to reach 0:00.
  • The Axiom: "Wicks do the damage (sweeps); bodies tell the truth (delivery)."

docs.title: 2. Fighting the Higher Timeframe Bias
docs.text:
• If the Daily and 4-Hour candles are in aggressive bearish delivery (creating lower lows and lower highs), do not trade bullish 1-minute reversals unless price has tapped a significant HTF Point of Interest.
  • Always check the HTF Candle Projection cluster on the right side of your chart before entering.

docs.title: 3. Widening Your Stop Loss Beyond C2
docs.text:
• In the Fractal Model, the lowest point of the C2 manipulation wick (c2_low for bullish, c2_high for bearish) is the absolute invalidation barrier.
  • If price violates C2 by even 1 tick, the entire setup premise has failed.
  • Never move your stop loss further away. Take the predefined loss and wait for the next setup.

docs.title: 4. Chasing the C3 Candle (FOMO)
docs.text:
• When C3 opens and expands rapidly, retail traders experience extreme FOMO and enter at the highest point of the candle.
  • Institutions will then initiate a pullback to retest the 50% equilibrium or CISD line, stopping out late buyers.
  • The Rule: If you missed the Model 1 CISD breakout close or the Model 2 T-Spot limit, let C3 close and look for a Model 4 continuation entry on C4!

docs.title: 5. Overtrading Outside Institutional Killzones
docs.text:
• The Fractal Model requires institutional volume to achieve directional displacement.
  • Trading during the dead lunch hour (12:00 – 13:30 NY Time) or late afternoon post-settlement leads to choppy ranges and false breakouts.
  • Stick strictly to London Open (02:00–05:00 NY) and New York AM (08:30–11:00 NY).

docs.title: 2. Daylight Saving Time (DST) Desynchronization Week
docs.text: Twice every year, international daylight saving rules cause a 1-week or 2-week time difference: - Fall (Late October / Early November): Europe ends British Summer Time (BST) / Central European Summer Time (CEST) on the last Sunday of October, while the United States does not fall back until the first Sunday of November. - Spring (March): The United States springs forward 2-3 weeks before Europe.

docs.title: What Happens During the Fall DST Gap Week:
docs.text: During this week: - London Session in New York Time: Shifts by 1 hour to 03:00 – 06:00 NY Time (or 03:00–07:00). - London Session in Local Ethiopia Time: The physical London morning does not change; it opens at 07:00 London Time. However, relative to New York clocks, London starts 1 hour later (at 03:00 NY time instead of 02:00 NY time). - C2 Candle Alignment: For London session traders using the 1-hour chart, the C2 manipulation candle during this week is the 03:00 – 04:00 candle, rather than the standard 02:00 – 03:00 candle! - NY Cash Open (09:30 NY): Still occurs at 09:30 NY Time (which aligns to 04:30 PM in Ethiopia).

docs.title: 2. Why "1m - 1H" is Mathematically Invalid for Model 1

The 60:1 Timeframe Ratio Trap

A common beginner error is trying to pair a 1-Hour candle as C2 with a 1-Minute chart for Model 1 (candle close) execution:

  • The 60-Minute Lag: Waiting 60 minutes for a 1-Hour candle to close means 60 individual 1-minute bars have already elapsed.
  • Premature Delivery: In London Open Forex, the entire Asian range sweep and directional run often takes only 25 to 40 minutes.
  • By the time the 1-Hour candle closes, the move has already reached its opposing Draw on Liquidity (DOL).
  • When the next 1-Hour candle (C3) opens, institutional orderflow takes profits and retraces, causing traders who wait for the 1H close to enter at the very ceiling/floor right as price reverses!

Rule 1: Time Dictates Price

Rule 3: Higher Timeframe Determines the Direction

Never trade a Lower Timeframe (LTF) signal in isolation. If the 4H or 1H candle is currently forming its C2 manipulation wick, you only look for LTF entries in the direction of the expected C3 expansion.

docs.title: 1. The Core Philosophy of Market Delivery
docs.text: The TTrades Fractal Model is predicated on the foundational tenet that financial markets do not move randomly; they deliver price algorithmically based on liquidity and orderflow imbalances.

docs.title: "Wicks Do the Damage, Bodies Tell the Story"
docs.text:
This ICT maxim is the bedrock of candle interpretation in the Fractal Model:

  • The Candle Body (Close vs Open): Represents true institutional volume and conviction. Where the candle body closes tells you whether algorithmic delivery was accepted or rejected at that price level.
  • The Candle Wick (High and Low): Represents liquidity probes, sweeps, and stop hunts. A wick extending past a level without candle body acceptance indicates orders were filled and price was immediately rejected.

docs.title: 2. Sweeps vs. Closes: Determining Market Intent
docs.text:
When price reaches an established swing high, session boundary, or key level, it interacts in one of two distinct algorithmic modes:

docs.title: 3. Dealing Ranges & The 50% Equilibrium (T-Spot)
docs.text: Every high-probability trade setup exists inside an active Dealing Range (the swing high and swing low defining current institutional price delivery).

docs.title: The Mathematical Formula:
docs.text:
Equilibrium = (Dealing_Range_High + Dealing_Range_Low) / 2
  • Wholesale Discount (< 50%): Institutional buy programs only execute when price trades below equilibrium into discount arrays (FVG, Orderblock, C2 Low).
  • Expensive Premium (> 50%): Institutional sell programs distribute long positions or open short positions when price trades above equilibrium.
  • TTrades Nuance:
    • During strong institutional expansions, price respects the 50% equilibrium line.
    • If a bullish displacement holds above 50% of the manipulation leg, the institutional orderbook remains fiercely protected by buyers.

docs.title: 4. Internal vs. External Liquidity Delivery (ERL to IRL)
docs.text:
Price perpetually cycles between two states of liquidity:

  1. External Range Liquidity (ERL):
    • Major swing highs, swing lows, and session extremes (Previous Day High/Low, London Session High/Low, Asian Session High/Low).
    • Once ERL is purged via a sweep, price seeks Internal Range Liquidity (IRL).
  2. Internal Range Liquidity (IRL):
    • Fair Value Gaps (FVG), Balanced Price Ranges (BPR), and Orderblocks inside the range.
    • Once IRL is rebalanced/mitigated, price spools back to seek opposing ERL.

The Master Execution Formula

We wait for an ERL sweep (forming a C2 candle), look for mitigation inside an IRL Point of Interest (the T-Spot / FVG), and ride the C3 expansion into opposing ERL.

docs.title: Candle 1 (C1) — The Reference Anchor
docs.text:
• Role: Sets the liquidity bounds and benchmark levels for the upcoming delivery cycle.

docs.title: Candle 2 (C2) — The Liquidity Sweep & Pivot Formation
docs.text:
• Role: The pivot candidate. C2 tests or purges the liquidity established by C1.
  • Bullish Setup Requirements:
    • C2 wicks below the C1 Low (sweeping sellside liquidity).
    • C2 candle body closes back inside the C1 range or above the sweep level.
    • The lowest point of C2 becomes the Extreme Low (c2_extreme), serving as the strict stop-loss invalidation level.
  • Bearish Setup Requirements:
    • C2 wicks above the C1 High (sweeping buyside liquidity).
    • C2 candle body closes back inside the C1 range or below the sweep level.
    • The highest point of C2 becomes the Extreme High (c2_extreme), serving as the strict stop-loss invalidation level.
  • Confirmation Rule: C2 is only an official pivot after it closes. If C2 is still open, it is treated as an active unconfirmed probe.

docs.title: Candle 3 (C3) — The Execution & Expansion Candle

• Role: The primary execution candle. This is where Power of 3 (Accumulation-Manipulation-Distribution) delivers explosive, directional displacement.
  • Execution Rules:

    • Retraces into the 50% T-Spot Zone or lower-timeframe discount FVG.
    • Confirms via a lower-timeframe Change in State of Delivery (CISD).
    • Expands aggressively toward the projected target liquidity.

docs.title: Candle 4 (C4) — The Delivery & Extension Candle

  • Rules:

    • Once price reaches -2.0 or -2.5 standard deviations, runner targets are closed or stop loss is trailed tightly.

docs.title: 1. What is a Change in State of Delivery (CISD)?
docs.text:
Change in State of Delivery (CISD) is the objective algorithmic confirmation mechanism of the TTrades Fractal Model.

In institutional market making algorithms: * When price is dropping into a sweep, every consecutive candle is delivered under a sell program (bearish institutional orderflow). * For the algorithm to legally shift into a buy program (bullish delivery), price must actively displace and close a candle body past the exact price origin where the final sell program initiated. * That origin point is mathematically and visually defined as the Open price of the first opposing candle in the leg that created the C2 extreme.

docs.title: 2. Technical Anatomy: Wick Rejection vs. Body Close
docs.text:
The single most critical rule in the entire framework: A wick piercing through the CISD line is NOT a valid trigger. Only a solid candle body close confirms that orderflow has flipped.

Below is the technical deep-dive chart contrasting a retail wick trap with a true algorithmic body close:

docs.title: The Golden Rule of the Benchmark Origin
docs.text:
Exact Origin Coordinate of the CISD Benchmark Line

The CISD horizontal ray must start visually and mathematically at the exact Open of the first opposing candle that initiated the final delivery leg into the C2 extreme:

  • Bullish CISD: The ray begins at the Open of the first bearish (down-close) candle that led down into the C2 sweep low.
  • Bearish CISD: The ray begins at the Open of the first bullish (up-close) candle that led up into the C2 sweep high.

docs.title: Bullish CISD Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Identify the Extreme: Locate the lowest point formed during the C2 liquidity sweep (c2_low).
  2. Trace Back the Bearish Leg: Locate the series of down-close (bearish) candles that drove price into that low.
  3. Anchor the Benchmark: Find the first candle of that bearish sequence. Place the horizontal CISD ray directly at its Open price.
  4. Wait for Candle Close: Monitor the execution timeframe (e.g. 1-minute chart).
  5. Trigger Validation: The candle body must close strictly above this benchmark line.

docs.title: Bearish CISD Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Identify the Extreme: Locate the highest point formed during the C2 liquidity sweep (c2_high).
  2. Trace Back the Bullish Leg: Locate the series of up-close (bullish) candles that drove price into that high.
  3. Anchor the Benchmark: Find the first candle of that bullish sequence. Place the horizontal CISD ray directly at its Open price.
  4. Trigger Validation: The candle body must close strictly below this benchmark line.

docs.title: 4. Early CISD vs. Confirmed CISD
docs.text:
In both live trading and the Pine Script indicator engine, two distinct stages of CISD exist:

CISD State Definition & Timing Risk Profile Best Use Case Early / Live CISD Triggers while C2 is still actively forming (intra-bar). Price sweeps C1 and breaks the opposing open before C2's HTF time closes. Higher reward, higher risk. If C2 expands further, the level can get invalidated. Scalpers seeking sniper entries at the HTF wick turn. Confirmed CISD Triggers after C2 has officially closed as a valid sweep. C3 opens and breaks the CISD level, or respects the already-broken level. High probability, conservative. C2 pivot is permanently locked in. Standard rule-based execution for consistent 70%+ win rates.

docs.text:
A CISD is declared INVALID immediately under any of these conditions:

  1. Wick-Only Piercing: Price wicks past the benchmark line but pulls back to close on the wrong side. Never enter on a wick probe.
  2. C2 Extreme Pierced: If price breaks the CISD line but subsequently reverses and violates the C2 sweep extreme by even 1 tick, the setup is DEAD. Close the trade immediately.
  3. Time Degradation: More than two higher timeframe candles elapse without directional displacement out of the CISD zone.

docs.title: 2. What is the "T-Spot"?
docs.text: The T-Spot is TTrades' proprietary calculation representing the exact zone where the higher-timeframe candle wick is anticipated to exhaust and reverse during the C3 expansion.

docs.title: Mathematical Derivation of the T-Spot
docs.text:
The T-Spot zone is calculated by taking the relationship between:

  1. The C2 Wick Midpoint (Equilibrium): 
    c2_wick_midpoint = (c2_high + c2_low) / 2
  2. The C3 Opening Price: 
    c3_open = open[0]  // at the start of C3
  3. The T-Spot Entry Zone:
    • For Bullish Setups: The box bounded between c3_open and c2_wick_midpoint (discount zone below 50% of the sweep leg).
    • For Bearish Setups: The box bounded between c3_open and c2_wick_midpoint (premium zone above 50% of the sweep leg).

docs.text:
When C3 opens, novice traders frequently chase the move immediately with aggressive market orders. However, institutional algorithms follow the Power of 3 (Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution):

  1. Open: C3 opens.
  2. Manipulation (Wick into T-Spot):

    • This shakes out early breakout buyers and fills institutional long limit orders at a superior wholesale discount.
  3. Distribution (Body Expansion):

docs.title: 1. What You See on the Indicator
docs.text:
When running the Fractal Model Pro+ [v6] indicator on your chart, Model 1 presents the following visual sequence:

  1. C1 Range Marked: Dotted bounds marking prior session or swing high/low.
  2. C2 Sweep Detected: Price wicks past C1 into an HTF discount POI, and the indicator places a label at the extreme.
  3. CISD Benchmark Line Appears: A solid horizontal ray originates strictly from the Open of the first opposing candle that led into the C2 extreme:
    • Blue Line: Bullish CISD benchmark level (Open of the first down-close candle into C2 low).
    • Red Line: Bearish CISD benchmark level (Open of the first up-close candle into C2 high).
  4. Dashboard State: The live HUD changes status from C2 Sweep to Watching CISD Level.

docs.title: Bullish Execution:
docs.text:
1. Pre-condition: C2 sweeps sellside liquidity (SSL) into an HTF Point of Interest (FVG or Orderblock) and prints a rejection wick.
  2. Watch the Benchmark Origin: Verify the blue CISD line originates at the Open of the first bearish candle into the C2 low.
  3. Wait for Candle Close: Watch the 1-minute candle timer countdown to 0:00.
  4. Trigger: The candle body must close strictly ABOVE the blue line.
  5. Entry:
    • Market Order: Click Buy Market the exact second the candle closes.
    • Retest Limit: Place a limit buy order directly on the blue line. Often the next candle dips 1-2 ticks to touch the line.
  6. Stop Loss: 1-2 ticks below the lowest wick tip of C2.
  7. Take Profit:
    • TP1 (-1.0 Ext / BSL): Take 50% partial profits and move stop loss to Break-Even.
    • TP2 (-2.0 to -2.5 Ext): Take 40% profits.
    • Runner (-4.0 Ext): Leave 10% runner.

docs.title: 4. Invalidation & Common Mistakes
docs.text:
Never Enter on a Wick Probe!

If a candle wicks through the blue CISD line by 10 points but pulls back and closes below the line, this is NOT an entry. Wicks without body closes represent liquidity rejection, and price will frequently drop lower to take out the C2 low!

Invalidation Stop

If price breaks the CISD line but subsequently rolls over and pierces the C2 extreme by even 1 tick, the setup is DEAD. Close the trade immediately. Never hold through an invalidation.

1. Pre-condition: C2 has closed as a valid sweep, and HTF bias is bullish.
  2. The Box Appears: At the opening bell of C3 (e.g. at 09:30 or on the hourly open), the green T-Spot box projects forward.
  3. Place the Limit Order:

  4. Passive Fill:

    • Price dips into discount, tags your limit order, and absorbs institutional liquidity.
  5. Stop Loss (SL):
    • Tight Stop: 1–2 ticks below the dotted equilibrium line (or bottom of the box).
    • Structural Stop: Below the lowest wick tip of C2.
  6. Take Profit (TP):

Incredible Risk-to-Reward

Because your stop loss is anchored to a discount level rather than a breakout high, your stop distance is often 50–70% smaller than Model 1. This allows substantially higher position sizing while keeping absolute risk fixed at 1%!

Missed Fill Risk

On ultra-violent trend days, price may only dip 2–3 ticks into the box before rocketing, leaving your limit order unfilled. If this happens, do not chase; wait for Model 4!

docs.text:
Model 4 is designed specifically to prevent traders from FOMO buying at the peak of an explosive expansion:

  1. C3 Closes Strong: A massive green displacement candle closes near its high, having broken above C1 high.
  2. C4 Opens: The indicator places a label C4 and projects the C4 Continuation Support Zone.
  3. Midpoint Dotted Line: Represents the 50.00% Equilibrium of the preceding C3 candle.
  4. Dashboard State: Bottom-right HUD displays C4 Trend Distribution.

docs.title: Bullish Execution:
docs.text:
1. The Mistake to Avoid:
    • Never buy at the peak of C3. Wait for C3 to close.
  2. The Pullback:
    • When C4 opens, price naturally pulls back as algorithms rebalance early longs.
    • Price dips to retest the broken C1 high (turned institutional support) or C3 Fair Value Gap.
  3. The Trigger:
    • Enter long as price tests the top of the C1 range or the 50% midpoint of C3.
    • Alternatively, enter on the close of the first 1m green candle that rejects the C4 box.
  4. Stop Loss (SL):
    • Placed 1–2 ticks below the 50% midpoint dotted line of C3 (or below the C4 pullback wick).
  5. Take Profit (TP):
    • Target the -2.0 and -4.0 Macro Standard Deviation extensions.
